units.zh: 王肅，字恭懿，琅邪臨沂人，司馬衍丞相導之後也。

translations.literal: Wang Su, styled Gongyi, was a man of Linyi in Langye, a descendant of Chancellor Dao under Emperor Xiaowu (Sima Yan).
translations.idiomatic: Wang Su, whose courtesy name was Gongyi, came from Linyi in Langye and was a descendant of Chancellor Wang Dao, who had served under Emperor Xiaowu (Sima Yan).

units.zh: 父奐，蕭賾尚書左僕射。

translations.literal: His father Huan was Left Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat under Xiao Ze.
translations.idiomatic: His father Wang Huan had served Xiao Ze as Left Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat.

units.zh: 十八年，與閻寶討張文禮，為馬軍都將。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year, with Yan Bao he campaigned against Zhang Wenli and served as commander of the horse army.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighteenth year he joined Yan Bao in the campaign against Zhang Wenli as commander of the horse army.

units.zh: 八月，收趙州，獲刺史王鋋。

translations.literal: In the eighth month he recovered Zhaozhou and captured the prefect Wang Rong.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month he recovered Zhaozhou and captured Prefect Wang Rong.

units.zh: 進逼鎮州，為流矢所中，卒於軍，時年四十六。

translations.literal: Advancing to press Zhenzhou, he was struck by a stray arrow and died in the army, aged forty-six.
translations.idiomatic: As he pressed the attack on Zhenzhou, a stray arrow struck him and he died in camp at forty-six.

translations.literal: Biographies, number fifty.
translations.idiomatic: the 50th year of Biographies

units.zh: 范岫傅昭孔休源江革徐勉許懋殷鈞

translations.literal: Fan Xia, Fu Zhao, Kong Xiuyuan, Jiang Ge, Xu Mian, Xu Mao, Yin Jun.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Xia, Fu Zhao, Kong Xiuyuan, Jiang Ge, Xu Mian, Xu Mao, and Yin Jun

units.zh: 永明中，魏使至，詔妙選朝士有辭辯者，接使於界首，故以岫兼淮陰長史迎焉。

translations.literal: In the Yongming era, when a Wei envoy arrived, an edict finely selected court officials with eloquence to receive the envoy at the border; therefore Xia was appointed concurrently chief clerk of Huaiyin to welcome him.
translations.idiomatic: During the Yongming era, when an envoy from Wei arrived, the court was ordered to select the most eloquent officials to receive him at the border. Xia was therefore appointed concurrently chief clerk of Huaiyin to welcome the envoy.

units.zh: 入為尚書左丞。

translations.literal: He entered the capital and became Left Assistant Director of the Imperial Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled to the capital and appointed Left Assistant Director of the Imperial Secretariat.

units.zh: 丁母憂，居喪過禮。

translations.literal: Upon his mother's death he entered mourning and observed it beyond the rites.
translations.idiomatic: When his mother died, he entered mourning and observed the rites with exceptional devotion.

units.zh: 永元末，為輔國將軍、冠軍晉安王長史，行南徐州事。

translations.literal: At the end of Yongyuan, he was General Who Assists the State, chief clerk to Prince Jin'an of Champion, and acted in the affairs of South Xuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Yongyuan era, he served as General Who Assists the State and chief clerk to Prince Jin'an of Champion, administering the affairs of South Xuzhou.

units.zh: 梁武帝平建鄴，承制徵為尚書吏部郎，參大選。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wu of Liang pacified Jiankang, by provisional order he was summoned as Director of the Personnel Bureau of the Imperial Secretariat and took part in the great selection.
translations.idiomatic: After Emperor Wu of Liang captured Jiankang, he was summoned by provisional order to serve as Director of the Personnel Bureau and to participate in the chief appointments of officials.

units.zh: 天監五年，為散騎常侍、光祿大夫，侍皇太子，給扶。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Tianjian, he was Regular Attendant and Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, attending the crown prince, with a staff granted.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Tianjian, he was appointed Regular Attendant and Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, attending upon the crown prince with a walking staff provided for his use.

units.zh: 尋為總明學士、奉朝請。

translations.literal: Soon he became a scholar of Zongming and Attendant at Court.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he was appointed a scholar of Zongming and Attendant at Court.

units.zh: 齊永明中，累遷尚書儀曹郎。

translations.literal: In the Yongming era of Qi, he was repeatedly promoted to Director of the Ceremonial Bureau of the Imperial Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: During the Yongming era of Qi, he rose through successive promotions to Director of the Ceremonial Bureau of the Imperial Secretariat.

units.zh: 先是御史中丞劉休薦昭于齊武帝，永明初，以昭為南郡王侍讀。

translations.literal: Earlier, Censor-in-Chief Liu Xiu had recommended Zhao to Emperor Wu of Qi; at the beginning of Yongming, Zhao was made Reader-in-Attendance to the Prince of Nanjun.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Censor-in-Chief Liu Xiu had recommended Zhao to Emperor Wu of Qi. At the beginning of the Yongming era, Zhao was appointed Reader-in-Attendance to the Prince of Nanjun.

units.zh: 常插燭板床，明帝聞之，賜漆合燭盤，敕曰：「卿有古人之風，故賜卿古人之物。」

translations.literal: He often stuck candles into a plain board bed. When Emperor Ming heard of this, he granted him a lacquered candle holder and tray, instructing: "You have the air of the ancients; therefore I grant you the things of the ancients."
translations.idiomatic: He often stuck candles into a plain wooden bed. When Emperor Ming heard of this, he sent him a lacquered candle holder and tray with the message, "You have the spirit of the ancients, so I give you the furnishings of the ancients."

units.zh: 累遷尚書左丞。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to Left Assistant Director of the Imperial Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He was subsequently promoted to Left Assistant Director of the Imperial Secretariat.

units.zh: 梁武帝素重昭，梁台建，以為給事黃門侍郎，領著作，兼御史中丞。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu of Liang had long esteemed Zhao. When the Liang administration was established, he was made Supervisor of Attendants and Gentleman of the Yellow Gate, concurrently overseeing the Bureau of Compilation and serving as Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu of Liang had long held Zhao in high regard. When the Liang administration was established, he appointed him Supervisor of Attendants and Gentleman of the Yellow Gate, concurrently overseeing the Bureau of Compilation and serving as Censor-in-Chief.

units.zh: 乃命去檻阱，猛獸竟不為害。

translations.literal: He then ordered the traps removed, and the fierce beasts in the end did no harm.
translations.idiomatic: He then ordered the traps removed, and the fierce beasts ceased to cause harm.

units.zh: 曆秘書監，太常卿，遷臨海太守。

translations.literal: He successively served as Director of the Palace Library and Minister of Ceremonies, then was transferred to Administrator of Linhai.
translations.idiomatic: He successively served as Director of the Palace Library and Minister of Ceremonies, then was transferred to Administrator of Linhai.

units.zh: 郡有蜜岩，前後太守皆自封固，專收其利。

translations.literal: The commandery had a Honey Cliff; successive administrators all sealed and enclosed it, monopolizing its profits.
translations.idiomatic: The commandery had a Honey Cliff that successive administrators had sealed off for their private profit.

units.zh: 卒，諡曰貞。

translations.literal: When he died, his posthumous title was Zhen.
translations.idiomatic: When he died, he was given the posthumous name Zhen.

units.zh: 長子諝，位尚書郎，湘東王外兵參軍。

translations.literal: His eldest son Xu held the post of Director of the Imperial Secretariat and Military Affairs Aide to the Prince of Xiangdong.
translations.idiomatic: His eldest son Xu served as Director of the Imperial Secretariat and Military Affairs Aide to the Prince of Xiangdong.

units.zh: 諝子准有文才，梁宣帝時，位度支尚書。

translations.literal: Xu's son Zhun had literary talent; in the time of Emperor Xuan of Liang he held the post of Minister of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: Xu's son Zhun was a man of literary talent who, under Emperor Xuan of Liang, served as Minister of Revenue.

units.zh: 子弘。

translations.literal: His son was Hong.
translations.idiomatic: His son was Hong.

units.zh: 孔休源字慶緒，會稽山陰人，晉尚書沖之八世孫，沖即開府儀同三司愉之世父也。

translations.literal: Kong Xiuyuan, styled Qingxu, was a native of Shanyin in Kuaiji, eighth-generation descendant of Chongzhi, Director of the Imperial Secretariat of Jin; Chong was the paternal uncle by generation of Yu, Grand Minister with Honors Equal to the Three Excellencies.
translations.idiomatic: Kong Xiuyuan, styled Qingxu, was a native of Shanyin in Kuaiji and an eighth-generation descendant of Chongzhi, Director of the Imperial Secretariat under the Jin dynasty. Chong was the paternal uncle of Yu, who held the rank of Grand Minister with Honors Equal to the Three Excellencies.

units.zh: 曾祖遙之，宋尚書水部郎。

translations.literal: His great-grandfather was Yaozhi, Director of the Water Bureau of the Imperial Secretariat under Song.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather Yaozhi served as Director of the Water Bureau of the Imperial Secretariat under the Song dynasty.

units.zh: 父佩，齊通直郎。

translations.literal: His father Pei was Attendant for Direct Communication under Qi.
translations.idiomatic: His father Pei served as Attendant for Direct Communication under the Qi dynasty.

units.zh: 梁台建，與南陽劉之遴同為太學博士，當時以為美選。

translations.literal: When the Liang administration was established, he and Liu Zhilin of Nanyang both served as erudites of the Imperial University; at the time this was considered a fine selection.
translations.idiomatic: When the Liang administration was established, he and Liu Zhilin of Nanyang were both appointed erudites of the Imperial University, a pairing widely regarded as an excellent choice.

units.zh: 休源初到都，寓於宗人少府孔登。

translations.literal: When Xiuyuan first arrived in the capital, he lodged with his clansman Kong Deng, Director of the Palace Treasury.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiuyuan first arrived in the capital, he stayed with his clansman Kong Deng, Director of the Palace Treasury.

units.zh: 曾以祠事入廟，侍中範雲一與相遇，深加褒賞，曰：「不期忽覯清顏，頓祛鄙吝，觀天披霧，驗之今日。」

translations.literal: Once, on temple business he entered the shrine and chanced to meet Attendant-in-Ordinary Fan Yun, who deeply praised him, saying: "Unexpectedly I suddenly behold your clear countenance; at once my vulgar parsimony is dispelled. To view heaven through parting clouds—today I verify it."
translations.idiomatic: Once, while entering a shrine on temple business, he chanced to meet Attendant-in-Ordinary Fan Yun, who praised him warmly, saying, "I never expected to meet you here. Your presence dispels my petty narrowness at once. It is like seeing the sky through parting clouds—and today I have proved it."

units.zh: 登深以為愧。

translations.literal: Deng was deeply ashamed.
translations.idiomatic: Kong Deng was deeply ashamed.

units.zh: 尚書令沈約當朝貴顯，軒蓋盈門，休源或時後來，必虛襟引接，處之坐右，商略文義。

translations.literal: Director of the Imperial Secretariat Shen Yue was eminent and honored in the court; carriages filled his gate. When Xiuyuan sometimes came later, Yue always received him with open heart, seated him at his right, and discussed literary meaning.
translations.idiomatic: Director of the Imperial Secretariat Shen Yue was one of the most eminent men at court, and carriages filled his gate. Whenever Xiuyuan arrived late, Yue received him with open warmth, seated him at his right hand, and discussed literature with him.

units.zh: 其為通人所推如此。

translations.literal: This was how he was esteemed by men of understanding.
translations.idiomatic: Such was the esteem in which men of discernment held him.

units.zh: 武帝嘗問吏部尚書徐勉求一有學藝解朝儀者，為尚書儀曹郎，勉曰：「孔休源識見清通，詳練故事，自晉、宋起居注，誦略上口。」

translations.literal: Emperor Wu once asked Minister of the Personnel Bureau Xu Mian to find someone learned in arts who understood court ritual to serve as Director of the Ceremonial Bureau. Mian said: "Kong Xiuyuan's knowledge and insight are clear and penetrating; he is thoroughly versed in precedents. From the Jin and Song daily records onward, he can recite them from memory."
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu once asked Minister of the Personnel Bureau Xu Mian to find a learned man who understood court ritual for the post of Director of the Ceremonial Bureau. Mian replied, "Kong Xiuyuan has clear and penetrating insight and is thoroughly versed in precedent. From the Jin and Song daily records onward, he can recite them from memory."

units.zh: 武帝亦素聞之，即日除兼尚書儀曹郎。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu had also long heard of him and that same day appointed him concurrently Director of the Ceremonial Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu had also long heard of him and appointed him that same day as concurrent Director of the Ceremonial Bureau.

units.zh: 時多所改作，每逮訪前事，休源即以所誦記隨機斷決，曾無疑滯。

translations.literal: At the time many reforms were made; whenever earlier matters were consulted, Xiuyuan would decide on the spot from what he had memorized, never hesitating.
translations.idiomatic: At the time many reforms were underway. Whenever earlier precedents were consulted, Xiuyuan decided on the spot from memory, never hesitating.

units.zh: 吏部郎任昉常謂之為「孔獨誦」。

translations.literal: Director of the Personnel Bureau Ren Fang often called him "Kong the Sole Reciter."
translations.idiomatic: Director of the Personnel Bureau Ren Fang often called him "Kong the Sole Reciter."

units.zh: 遷建康獄正，平反辯析，時罕冤人。

translations.literal: He was transferred to be Warden of Jiankang Prison, overturning wrongful verdicts and analyzing cases; at the time few innocent people suffered injustice.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Warden of Jiankang Prison, where he overturned wrongful verdicts and analyzed cases with such care that few innocent people were wronged.

units.zh: 除中書舍人。

translations.literal: He was appointed Attendant of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Attendant of the Secretariat.

units.zh: 後為尚書左丞，彈肅禮闈，雅允朝望。

translations.literal: Later he became Left Assistant Director of the Imperial Secretariat, enforcing discipline in the examination halls and fully meeting the court's expectations.
translations.idiomatic: He later served as Left Assistant Director of the Imperial Secretariat, enforcing discipline in the examination halls and fully meeting the court's expectations.

units.zh: 時周舍撰禮疑義，自漢、魏至於齊、梁，並皆搜采，休源所有奏議，咸預編錄。

translations.literal: At the time Zhou She compiled doubtful points in ritual, searching from Han and Wei through Qi and Liang; all of Xiuyuan's memorials and proposals were included in the compilation.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Zhou She was compiling doubtful points in ritual, gathering material from Han and Wei through Qi and Liang. All of Xiuyuan's memorials and proposals were included in the work.

units.zh: 帝深嘉之。

translations.literal: The emperor deeply praised him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor praised him highly.

units.zh: 曆秘書監，復為晉安王府長史、南蘭陵太守，別敕專行南徐州事。

translations.literal: He successively served as Director of the Palace Library, then again as chief clerk to Prince Jin'an's household and Administrator of Nanlanling, with a separate edict appointing him solely to administer South Xuzhou affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He successively served as Director of the Palace Library, then again as chief clerk to Prince Jin'an's household and Administrator of Nanlanling, with a separate edict appointing him solely to administer South Xuzhou affairs.

units.zh: 休源累佐名蕃，甚得人譽，王深相倚仗，常於中齋別施一榻，云：「此是孔長史坐」，人莫得預焉，其見敬如此。

translations.literal: Xiuyuan repeatedly assisted famous princely domains and won great public esteem. The prince deeply relied on him and always placed a separate couch in the inner study, saying: "This is Chief Clerk Kong's seat." No one else was permitted there; such was the respect shown him.
translations.idiomatic: Xiuyuan repeatedly assisted distinguished princely domains and won great public esteem. The prince relied on him deeply and always placed a separate couch in the inner study, saying, "This is Chief Clerk Kong's seat." No one else was permitted to use it; such was the respect shown him.

units.zh: 長子雲章頗有父風，位東揚州別駕。

translations.literal: His eldest son Yunzhang largely had his father's character and held the post of Vice Administrator of East Yangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: His eldest son Yunzhang largely inherited his father's character and served as Vice Administrator of East Yangzhou.

units.zh: 少子宗范聰敏有識度，位中書郎。

translations.literal: His younger son Zongfan was intelligent and perceptive and held the post of Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: His younger son Zongfan was intelligent and perceptive and served as Director of the Secretariat.

units.zh: 江革字休映，濟陽考城人也。

translations.literal: Jiang Ge, styled Xiuying, was a native of Kaocheng in Jiyang.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Ge, styled Xiuying, was a native of Kaocheng in Jiyang.

units.zh: 祖齊之，宋都水使者，尚書金部郎。

translations.literal: His grandfather was Qizhi, Commissioner of Waterways under Song and Director of the Gold Bureau of the Imperial Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Qizhi served as Commissioner of Waterways under the Song dynasty and as Director of the Gold Bureau of the Imperial Secretariat.

units.zh: 父柔之，齊尚書倉部郎，有孝行，以母憂毀卒。

translations.literal: His father Rouzhi was Director of the Granary Bureau of the Imperial Secretariat under Qi, a man of filial conduct who died from grief during his mother's mourning.
translations.idiomatic: His father Rouzhi served as Director of the Granary Bureau of the Imperial Secretariat under the Qi dynasty. A man of filial devotion, he died from grief during his mother's mourning period.

units.zh: 革幼而聰敏，早有才思，六歲便解屬文。

translations.literal: Ge from youth was intelligent and keen; early he had literary talent, and at six he could already compose prose.
translations.idiomatic: Ge was intelligent from childhood and showed early literary talent; at the age of six he could already compose prose.

units.zh: 服闋，與觀俱詣太學，補國子生，舉高第。

translations.literal: When mourning ended, he and Guan both went to the Imperial University, were enrolled as students of the National University, and were recommended with highest marks.
translations.idiomatic: When mourning ended, he and Guan both entered the Imperial University as students of the National University and were recommended with the highest marks.

units.zh: 齊中書郎王融、吏部郎謝朓雅相欽重。

translations.literal: Wang Rong, Director of the Secretariat under Qi, and Xie Tiao, Director of the Personnel Bureau, both deeply admired and esteemed him.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Rong, Director of the Secretariat under Qi, and Xie Tiao, Director of the Personnel Bureau, both deeply admired and esteemed him.

units.zh: 朓嘗行還過候革，時大寒雪，見革弊絮單席，而耽學不倦，嗟歎久之，乃脫其所著襦，並手割半氈與革充臥具而去。

translations.literal: Tiao once returned from a journey and stopped to visit Ge. It was bitterly cold with snow; he saw Ge in worn cotton and on a single mat, yet devoted to study without weariness. Tiao sighed long, then took off his own padded jacket and with his own hands cut half a felt rug to serve as Ge's bedding before departing.
translations.idiomatic: Tiao once returned from a journey and stopped to visit Ge. It was bitterly cold and snowing; he found Ge in worn cotton clothing on a single mat, yet still devoted to study without rest. Tiao sighed at length, then took off his own padded jacket and cut half a felt rug by hand to serve as Ge's bedding before departing.

units.zh: 諧之方貢琅邪王泛，便以革代之。

translations.literal: Xiezhi had just presented Wang Fan of Langya as tribute and therefore replaced him with Ge.
translations.idiomatic: Xiezhi had just presented Wang Fan of Langya as tribute and therefore substituted Ge in his place.

units.zh: 僕射江祏深相引接，祏為太子詹事，啟革為丞。

translations.literal: Vice Director Jiang Si deeply received and welcomed him. When Si became Supervisor of the Heir Apparent's Household, he recommended Ge as assistant.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Director Jiang Si received him warmly. When Si became Supervisor of the Heir Apparent's Household, he recommended Ge as assistant.

units.zh: 祏時權傾朝右，以革才堪經國，令參掌機務，詔誥文檄皆委以具。

translations.literal: At the time Si's power tilted the right side of the court; considering Ge's talent fit for governing the state, he had him take part in managing secret affairs. Edicts, proclamations, and dispatches were all entrusted to Ge to draft.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Si wielded enormous power at court. Considering Ge's talent fit for governing the state, he had him take part in managing secret affairs. Edicts, proclamations, and dispatches were all entrusted to Ge to draft.

units.zh: 祏誅，賓客皆罹其罪，革獨以智免。

translations.literal: When Si was executed, his retainers all suffered for the crime; Ge alone escaped through wisdom.
translations.idiomatic: When Si was executed, his retainers all suffered for the crime, but Ge alone escaped through his shrewdness.

units.zh: 除尚書駕部郎。

translations.literal: He was appointed Director of the Chariot Bureau of the Imperial Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Director of the Chariot Bureau of the Imperial Secretariat.

units.zh: 中興元年，梁武帝入石頭，時吳興太守袁昂據郡拒義不從，革制書與昂，于坐立成，辭義典雅，帝深賞歎之，令與徐勉同掌書記。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhongxing, Emperor Wu of Liang entered Shitou. At the time Yuan Ang, Administrator of Wuxing, held the commandery and refused to follow the righteous cause. Ge drafted a letter to Ang, completing it while seated; its language and meaning were elegant and classical. The emperor deeply admired it and ordered him to manage records together with Xu Mian.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Zhongxing, Emperor Wu of Liang entered Shitou. At the time Yuan Ang, Administrator of Wuxing, held the commandery and refused to submit. Ge drafted a letter to Ang, completing it while seated; its language and meaning were elegant and classical. The emperor admired it deeply and ordered him to manage records together with Xu Mian.

units.zh: 建安王為雍州刺史，表求管記，以革為征北記室參軍，帶中廬令。

translations.literal: Prince Jian'an became Governor of Yongzhou and memorialized requesting a records officer; Ge was made Military Affairs Secretary to the Campaign North and concurrently Director of the Central Stable.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Jian'an became Governor of Yongzhou and memorialized requesting a records officer. Ge was appointed Military Affairs Secretary to the Campaign North and concurrently Director of the Central Stable.

units.zh: 與弟觀少長共居，不忍離別，苦求同行。

translations.literal: He and his younger brother Guan had lived together from youth to adulthood and could not bear to part; he earnestly begged to travel together.
translations.idiomatic: He and his younger brother Guan had lived together from youth and could not bear to part; he earnestly begged to travel together.

units.zh: 後為建康正，頻遷秣陵、建康令，為政明肅，豪強憚之。

translations.literal: Later he was Warden of Jiankang, then repeatedly promoted to magistrate of Moling and Jiankang; his governance was clear and stern, and the powerful feared him.
translations.idiomatic: He later served as Warden of Jiankang, then was repeatedly promoted to magistrate of Moling and Jiankang. His governance was clear and stern, and the powerful feared him.

units.zh: 曆中書舍人，尚書左丞，晉安王長史、尋陽太守，行江州府事。

translations.literal: He successively served as Attendant of the Secretariat, Left Assistant Director of the Imperial Secretariat, chief clerk to Prince Jin'an, Administrator of Xunyang, and administered the affairs of Jiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He successively served as Attendant of the Secretariat, Left Assistant Director of the Imperial Secretariat, chief clerk to Prince Jin'an, Administrator of Xunyang, and administrator of Jiangzhou affairs.

units.zh: 徙廬陵王長史，太守、行事如故。

translations.literal: He was transferred to chief clerk to the Prince of Luling; his posts as Administrator and acting affairs remained as before.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to chief clerk to the Prince of Luling, retaining his posts as Administrator and acting affairs.

units.zh: 每侍燕，言論必以詩、書，王因此耽學好文。

translations.literal: Whenever he attended banquets, his discourse always drew on the Book of Songs and the Book of Documents; because of this the prince became devoted to study and fond of literature.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever he attended banquets, his discourse always drew on the Book of Songs and the Book of Documents. Because of this the prince became devoted to study and fond of literature.

units.zh: 典簽沈熾文以王所制詩呈武帝，帝謂僕射徐勉曰：「革果稱職。」

translations.literal: Chief Clerk Shen Chiwen presented to Emperor Wu poems composed by the prince. The emperor said to Vice Director Xu Mian: "Ge truly fills his post."
translations.idiomatic: Chief Clerk Shen Chiwen presented to Emperor Wu poems composed by the prince. The emperor said to Vice Director Xu Mian, "Ge truly fills his post."

units.zh: 乃除都官尚書。

translations.literal: He then appointed him Minister of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: He then appointed him Minister of Justice.

units.zh: 好獎進閭閻，為後生延譽，由是衣冠士子翕然歸之。

translations.literal: He loved to encourage and advance men of the lanes and wards, extending reputation for younger generations; thereby gentry and scholars converged upon him.
translations.idiomatic: He loved to encourage and advance men of the lanes and wards, extending reputation for younger generations. Thereby gentry and scholars converged upon him.

units.zh: 時尚書令何敬容掌選，序用多非其人。

translations.literal: At the time Director of the Imperial Secretariat He Jingrong managed selection, and many of those he appointed in order were not the right men.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Director of the Imperial Secretariat He Jingrong managed selection, and many of those he appointed were not the right men.

units.zh: 革性強直，每朝宴恒有褒貶，以此為權貴所疾。

translations.literal: Ge's nature was forceful and upright; at every court banquet he always had praise and blame, and for this was resented by the powerful and noble.
translations.idiomatic: Ge's nature was forceful and upright. At every court banquet he always had praise and blame to offer, and for this the powerful and noble resented him.

units.zh: 涉獵經籍，善屬文。

translations.literal: He ranged through the classics and was skilled at composing prose.
translations.idiomatic: He ranged through the classics and was skilled at composing prose.

units.zh: 仕梁為尚書比部郎，以父憂去職。

translations.literal: He served Liang as Director of the Comparison Bureau of the Imperial Secretariat and left office on his father's death.
translations.idiomatic: He served under Liang as Director of the Comparison Bureau of the Imperial Secretariat and left office on his father's death.

units.zh: 服闋後，容貌毀瘠，如居喪時。

translations.literal: After mourning ended, his appearance was wasted and gaunt, as though still in mourning.
translations.idiomatic: After mourning ended, his appearance remained wasted and gaunt, as though still in mourning.

units.zh: 及陳武帝受禪，為秘書監，兼尚書左丞。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wu of Chen accepted the abdication, he became Director of the Palace Library and concurrently Left Assistant Director of the Imperial Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wu of Chen accepted the abdication, he became Director of the Palace Library and concurrently Left Assistant Director of the Imperial Secretariat.

units.zh: 尋以本官兼中書舍人。

translations.literal: Soon, in his existing post, he additionally served as Attendant of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Soon, in his existing post, he additionally served as Attendant of the Secretariat.

units.zh: 天嘉中，兼散騎常侍，與中書郎劉師知使齊，著北征道里記三卷。

translations.literal: In the Tianjia era, he concurrently served as Regular Attendant and, with Director of the Secretariat Liu Shizhi, was envoy to Qi, composing the Record of Routes on the Northern Expedition in three scrolls.
translations.idiomatic: In the Tianjia era, he concurrently served as Regular Attendant and, with Director of the Secretariat Liu Shizhi, was envoy to Qi, composing the Record of Routes on the Northern Expedition in three scrolls.

units.zh: 還除太子中庶子。

translations.literal: Upon return he was appointed Supervisor of the Heir Apparent's Household.
translations.idiomatic: Upon return he was appointed Supervisor of the Heir Apparent's Household.

units.zh: 文筆十五卷。

translations.literal: His literary writings filled fifteen scrolls.
translations.idiomatic: His literary writings filled fifteen scrolls.

units.zh: 子椿亦善屬文，位尚書右丞。

translations.literal: His son Chun was also skilled at composing prose and held the post of Right Assistant Director of the Imperial Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: His son Chun was also skilled at composing prose and served as Right Assistant Director of the Imperial Secretariat.

units.zh: 德藻弟從簡，少有文情，年十七，作采荷調以刺何敬容，為當時所賞。

translations.literal: Dezao's younger brother Congjian had literary talent from youth. At seventeen he composed the Tune of Picking Lotus to satirize He Jingrong and was admired by contemporaries.
translations.idiomatic: Dezao's younger brother Congjian had literary talent from youth. At seventeen he composed the Tune of Picking Lotus to satirize He Jingrong and was admired by contemporaries.

units.zh: 初與長沙宣武王游，梁武帝深器賞之，及武帝兵至建鄴，勉于新林謁見，帝甚加恩禮，使管書記。

translations.literal: Early on he associated with Prince Xuanwu of Changsha; Emperor Wu of Liang deeply valued and admired him. When the emperor's army reached Jiankang, Mian paid his respects at Xinlin; the emperor greatly added favor and courtesy and had him manage records.
translations.idiomatic: Early on he associated with Prince Xuanwu of Changsha, and Emperor Wu of Liang deeply valued him. When the emperor's army reached Jiankang, Mian paid his respects at Xinlin. The emperor greatly honored him and had him manage records.

units.zh: 及帝即位，拜中書侍郎，進領中書通事舍人，直內省。

translations.literal: When the emperor ascended the throne, Mian was appointed Director of the Secretariat, then advanced to General Affairs Attendant of the Secretariat, serving in the inner office.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor ascended the throne, Mian was appointed Director of the Secretariat, then advanced to General Affairs Attendant of the Secretariat, serving in the inner office.

units.zh: 遷臨川王后軍諮議、尚書左丞。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Military Affairs Counselor to the Rear Army of Prince Linchuan and Left Assistant Director of the Imperial Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Military Affairs Counselor to the Rear Army of Prince Linchuan and Left Assistant Director of the Imperial Secretariat.

units.zh: 自掌樞憲，多所糾舉，時論以為稱職。

translations.literal: From managing the pivot of law and censure he impeached many; public opinion considered him fit for his post.
translations.idiomatic: From managing the pivot of law and censure he impeached many; public opinion considered him fit for his post.

units.zh: 天監三年，除給事黃門侍郎，尚書吏部郎，參掌大選。

translations.literal: In the third year of Tianjian, he was appointed Supervisor of Attendants and Gentleman of the Yellow Gate, Director of the Personnel Bureau, and took part in managing the great selection.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Tianjian, he was appointed Supervisor of Attendants and Gentleman of the Yellow Gate, Director of the Personnel Bureau, and took part in managing the great selection of officials.

units.zh: 遷侍中。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Attendant-in-Ordinary.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Attendant-in-Ordinary.

units.zh: 昭明太子尚幼，敕知宮事，太子禮之甚重，每事詢謀。

translations.literal: Crown Prince Zhaoming was still young; by edict Mian was ordered to manage palace affairs. The crown prince honored him greatly and consulted him on every matter.
translations.idiomatic: Crown Prince Zhaoming was still young. By edict Mian was ordered to manage palace affairs. The crown prince honored him greatly and consulted him on every matter.

units.zh: 嘗於殿講孝經，臨川王宏、尚書令沈約備二傅，勉與國子祭酒張充為執經，王瑩、張稷、柳憕、王暕為侍講。

translations.literal: Once in the hall he lectured on the Classic of Filial Piety. Prince Linchuan Hong and Director of the Imperial Secretariat Shen Yue served as the two mentors; Mian and Chancellor of the Imperial University Zhang Chong held the classic; Wang Ying, Zhang Ji, Liu Zong, and Wang Yan served as lecture attendants.
translations.idiomatic: Once in the hall he lectured on the Classic of Filial Piety. Prince Linchuan Hong and Director of the Imperial Secretariat Shen Yue served as the two mentors; Mian and Chancellor of the Imperial University Zhang Chong held the classic; Wang Ying, Zhang Ji, Liu Zong, and Wang Yan served as lecture attendants.

units.zh: 時選極親賢，妙盡人譽。

translations.literal: The selection at the time was of the closest kin and worthiest men, wonderfully exhausting human praise.
translations.idiomatic: The selection at the time drew on the closest kin and worthiest men, winning universal praise.

units.zh: 勉恥以其先為戲，答旨不恭，由是左遷散騎常侍，領遊擊將軍。

translations.literal: Mian was ashamed that his ancestors were made a jest; his reply to the edict was disrespectful, and for this he was demoted to Regular Attendant and concurrently General of the Mobile Corps.
translations.idiomatic: Mian was ashamed that his ancestors were made a jest. His reply to the edict was disrespectful, and for this he was demoted to Regular Attendant and concurrently General of the Mobile Corps.

units.zh: 後為太子詹事，又遷尚書右僕射，詹事如故。

translations.literal: Later he served as Supervisor of the Heir Apparent's Household, then was transferred to Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat, his post as Supervisor remaining as before.
translations.idiomatic: Later he served as Supervisor of the Heir Apparent's Household, then was transferred to Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat, retaining his post as Supervisor.

units.zh: 時人間喪事多不遵禮，朝終夕殯，相尚以速。

translations.literal: At the time funerals among the people often did not follow ritual; mourning ended in the morning and encoffining came in the evening, with speed mutually prized.
translations.idiomatic: At the time funerals among the people often did not follow ritual. Mourning ended in the morning and encoffining came in the evening, with speed mutually prized.

units.zh: 詔可其奏。

translations.literal: An edict approved his memorial.
translations.idiomatic: An edict approved his memorial.

units.zh: 又除尚書僕射、中衛將軍。

translations.literal: He was additionally appointed Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat and General of the Central Guard.
translations.idiomatic: He was additionally appointed Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat and General of the Central Guard.

units.zh: 勉以舊恩，繼升重位，盡心奉上，知無不為。

translations.literal: Mian, through old favor, rose in succession to heavy posts, devoting his heart in serving the sovereign, doing all he knew to do.
translations.idiomatic: Mian, through old favor, rose in succession to heavy posts, devoting his heart to serving the sovereign and doing all he knew to do.

units.zh: 及文憲薨，遺文散逸，又以事付國子祭酒何胤，經涉九載，猶復未畢。

translations.literal: When Wenxian died, surviving texts scattered and were lost. The task was again entrusted to Chancellor of the Imperial University He Yin; nine years passed, and it was still not finished.
translations.idiomatic: When Wenxian died, surviving texts scattered and were lost. The task was again entrusted to Chancellor of the Imperial University He Yin. Nine years passed, and it was still not finished.

units.zh: 建武四年，胤還東山，齊明帝敕委尚書令徐孝嗣，舊事本末，隨在南第。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Jianwu, Yin returned to East Mountain. Emperor Ming of Qi ordered that Director of the Imperial Secretariat Xu Xiaosi take charge; the origins and ends of old affairs followed him to the southern residence.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Jianwu, Yin returned to East Mountain. Emperor Ming of Qi ordered that Director of the Imperial Secretariat Xu Xiaosi take charge. The origins and ends of old affairs followed him to the southern residence.

units.zh: 永元中，孝嗣於此遇禍，又多零落。

translations.literal: In Yongyuan, Xiaosi met disaster here, and much more was scattered and lost.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongyuan, Xiaosi met disaster here, and much more was scattered and lost.

units.zh: 當時鳩集所余，權付尚書左丞蔡仲熊、驍騎將軍何佟之共掌其事。

translations.literal: At the time what remained was gathered together and provisionally entrusted to Left Assistant Director of the Imperial Secretariat Cai Zhongxiong and General of Valiant Cavalry He Tongzhi to manage the affair jointly.
translations.idiomatic: At the time what remained was gathered together and provisionally entrusted to Left Assistant Director of the Imperial Secretariat Cai Zhongxiong and General of Valiant Cavalry He Tongzhi to manage the affair jointly.

units.zh: 時禮局住在國子學中門外，東昏之時，頻有軍火，其所散失，又踰太半。

translations.literal: At the time the Ritual Bureau dwelt outside the middle gate of the Imperial University. In the time of Donghun there were frequent military fires; what was scattered and lost exceeded half again.
translations.idiomatic: At the time the Ritual Bureau dwelt outside the middle gate of the Imperial University. In the time of Donghun there were frequent military fires, and what was scattered and lost exceeded half again.

units.zh: 詔旨云：「禮壞樂缺，故國異家殊，實宜以時修定，以為永准。」

translations.literal: The edict's intent said: "Ritual is broken and music lacking, therefore states differ and families vary. It truly should be revised and fixed in season as an eternal standard."
translations.idiomatic: The edict's intent said, "Ritual is broken and music lacking, therefore states differ and families vary. It truly should be revised and fixed in season as an eternal standard."

units.zh: 於是尚書僕射沈約等參議，請五禮各置舊學士一人，人各自舉學士二人相助，抄撰其中。

translations.literal: Thereupon Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat Shen Yue and others jointly deliberated, requesting that each of the Five Rites have one old scholar appointed, each man recommending two scholars to assist, copying and compiling within them.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat Shen Yue and others jointly deliberated, requesting that each of the Five Rites have one old scholar appointed, each man recommending two scholars to assist in copying and compiling.

units.zh: 有疑者依前漢石渠、後漢白虎，隨源以聞，請旨斷決。

translations.literal: Where there were doubts, following the Stone Canal of Former Han and the White Tiger of Later Han, trace the source and report, requesting imperial decision.
translations.idiomatic: Where there were doubts, following the Stone Canal of Former Han and the White Tiger of Later Han, trace the source and report, requesting imperial decision.

units.zh: 乃以舊學士右軍記室參軍明山賓掌吉禮，中軍騎兵參軍嚴植之掌凶禮，中軍田曹行參軍兼太常丞賀瑒掌賓禮，征虜記室參軍陸璉掌軍禮，右軍參軍事司馬褧掌嘉禮，尚書右丞何佟之總參其事。

translations.literal: They then appointed old scholar Ming Shanbin, Military Affairs Secretary of the Right Army, to manage auspicious rites; Yan Zhizhi, Cavalry Military Affairs Aide of the Central Army, to manage inauspicious rites; He Yang, Acting Military Affairs Aide in the Field Bureau of the Central Army and concurrently Director of the Ministry of Ceremonies, to manage guest rites; Lu Lian, Military Affairs Secretary of the Campaign Against Barbarians, to manage military rites; Sima Jiong, Military Affairs Aide of the Right Army, to manage celebratory rites; and Right Assistant Director of the Imperial Secretariat He Tongzhi to oversee the affair in general.
translations.idiomatic: They then appointed old scholar Ming Shanbin, Military Affairs Secretary of the Right Army, to manage auspicious rites; Yan Zhizhi, Cavalry Military Affairs Aide of the Central Army, to manage inauspicious rites; He Yang, Acting Military Affairs Aide in the Field Bureau of the Central Army and concurrently Director of the Ministry of Ceremonies, to manage guest rites; Lu Lian, Military Affairs Secretary of the Campaign Against Barbarians, to manage military rites; Sima Jiong, Military Affairs Aide of the Right Army, to manage celebratory rites; and Right Assistant Director of the Imperial Secretariat He Tongzhi to oversee the affair in general.

units.zh: 佟之亡後，以鎮北諮議參軍伏揯代之。

translations.literal: After Tongzhi died, Fu Yin, Military Affairs Counselor of Campaign North, replaced him.
translations.idiomatic: After Tongzhi died, Fu Yin, Military Affairs Counselor of Campaign North, replaced him.

units.zh: 復以禮儀深廣，記載殘缺，宜須博論，共盡其致，更使鎮軍將軍丹陽尹沈約、太常卿張充及臣三人同參厥務，臣又奉別敕總知其事。

translations.literal: Again, because ritual propriety was deep and broad and records were fragmentary and incomplete, broad discussion was needed to exhaust its reach together. General of the Garrison Army and Prefect of Danyang Shen Yue, Minister of Ceremonies Zhang Chong, and your servant, three men, were further ordered to take part in the task jointly; your servant also received a separate edict to oversee the affair in general.
translations.idiomatic: Again, because ritual propriety was deep and broad and records were fragmentary and incomplete, broad discussion was needed to exhaust its reach together. General of the Garrison Army and Prefect of Danyang Shen Yue, Minister of Ceremonies Zhang Chong, and your servant, three men, were further ordered to take part in the task jointly. Your servant also received a separate edict to oversee the affair in general.

units.zh: 末又使中書侍郎周舍、庾於陵二人復豫參知。

translations.literal: Finally, Director of the Secretariat Zhou She and Yu Yuling, two men, were again ordered to take part in knowing the affair.
translations.idiomatic: Finally, Director of the Secretariat Zhou She and Yu Yuling, two men, were again ordered to take part in knowing the affair.

units.zh: 若有疑義，所掌學士當職先立議，通諮五禮舊學士及參知各言同異，條牒啟聞，決之制旨。

translations.literal: If there were doubtful points, the scholar in charge of the duty first established a proposal, consulted broadly with the old scholars of the Five Rites and those taking part in knowing, each stating agreement or difference, listed and reported upward, and decided by imperial intent.
translations.idiomatic: If there were doubtful points, the scholar in charge first established a proposal, consulted broadly with the old scholars of the Five Rites and those taking part in knowing, each stating agreement or difference, listed and reported upward, and decided by imperial intent.

units.zh: 詔有司案以遵行。

translations.literal: An edict ordered the relevant offices to examine and follow it in practice.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered the relevant offices to examine and follow it in practice.

units.zh: 尋加中書令，勉以疾求解內任，詔不許，乃令停下省，三日一朝，有事遣主書論決。

translations.literal: Soon he was additionally made Director of the Secretariat. Mian, because of illness, requested release from inner duties; an edict did not permit it, but ordered him to stop at the lower office, attend court once every three days, and when there were matters send the chief clerk to discuss and decide.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was additionally made Director of the Secretariat. Mian, because of illness, requested release from inner duties. An edict did not permit it, but ordered him to stop at the lower office, attend court once every three days, and when there were matters send the chief clerk to discuss and decide.

units.zh: 患腳轉劇，久闕朝覲，固陳求解，詔許疾差還省。

translations.literal: His foot ailment grew severe; long absent from court audience, he firmly memorialized requesting release. An edict permitted him to return to office when illness improved.
translations.idiomatic: His foot ailment grew severe. Long absent from court audience, he firmly memorialized requesting release. An edict permitted him to return to office when illness improved.

units.zh: 善屬文，勤著述，雖當機務，下筆不休。

translations.literal: Skilled at composing prose, diligent in writing, even when handling urgent affairs his brush did not stop.
translations.idiomatic: Skilled at composing prose and diligent in writing, even when handling urgent affairs his brush did not stop.

units.zh: 常以起居注煩雜，乃撰為流別起居注六百六十卷，左丞彈事五卷。

translations.literal: He often found the daily records troublesome and complex, and therefore compiled them into categorized daily records of six hundred sixty scrolls, and five scrolls of impeachments by the Left Assistant Director.
translations.idiomatic: He often found the daily records troublesome and complex, and therefore compiled them into categorized daily records of six hundred sixty scrolls, and five scrolls of impeachments by the Left Assistant Director.

units.zh: 在選曹，撰選品三卷。

translations.literal: In the Selection Bureau he compiled three scrolls of Selection Grades.
translations.idiomatic: In the Selection Bureau he compiled three scrolls of Selection Grades.

units.zh: 凡所著前後二集五十卷，又為人章表集十卷。

translations.literal: In all, his earlier and later two collections filled fifty scrolls; he also compiled ten scrolls of memorials for others.
translations.idiomatic: In all, his earlier and later two collections filled fifty scrolls. He also compiled ten scrolls of memorials for others.

units.zh: 大同三年，故佐史尚書左丞劉覽等詣闕陳勉行狀，請刊石紀德，即降詔立碑於墓焉。

translations.literal: In the third year of Datong, former assistant clerks including Left Assistant Director of the Imperial Secretariat Liu Lan went to the palace to present Mian's conduct report, requesting stone inscription to record virtue; an edict was immediately issued to erect a stele at the tomb.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Datong, former assistant clerks including Left Assistant Director of the Imperial Secretariat Liu Lan went to the palace to present Mian's conduct report, requesting stone inscription to record virtue. An edict was immediately issued to erect a stele at the tomb.

units.zh: 悱字敬業，幼聰敏，能屬文，位太子舍人，掌書記。

translations.literal: Fei, styled Jingye, was intelligent from youth and could compose prose. He held the post of Attendant of the Heir Apparent and managed records.
translations.idiomatic: Fei, styled Jingye, was intelligent from youth and could compose prose. He served as Attendant of the Heir Apparent and managed records.

units.zh: 五世祖詢，晉征士。

translations.literal: His fifth-generation ancestor Xun was a reclusive scholar of Jin.
translations.idiomatic: His fifth-generation ancestor Xun was a reclusive scholar under the Jin dynasty.

units.zh: 祖珪，宋給事中，著作郎，桂陽太守。

translations.literal: His grandfather Gui was Attendant at Court, Director of Compilation, and Administrator of Guiyang under Song.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Gui served as Attendant at Court, Director of Compilation, and Administrator of Guiyang under the Song dynasty.

units.zh: 父勇慧，齊太子家令，冗從僕射。

translations.literal: His father Yonghui was Steward of the Heir Apparent's Household and Supernumerary Vice Director of Retainers under Qi.
translations.idiomatic: His father Yonghui served as Steward of the Heir Apparent's Household and Supernumerary Vice Director of Retainers under the Qi dynasty.

units.zh: 懋少孤，性至孝，居父憂執喪過禮。

translations.literal: Mao was orphaned young, supremely filial by nature; in his father's mourning he observed the rites beyond measure.
translations.idiomatic: Mao was orphaned young and supremely filial by nature. In his father's mourning he observed the rites beyond measure.

units.zh: 後兼國子博士，與司馬褧同志友善。

translations.literal: Later he concurrently served as erudite of the National University and was of one intent and friendly with Sima Jiong.
translations.idiomatic: Later he concurrently served as erudite of the National University and was of one intent and friendly with Sima Jiong.

units.zh: 僕射江祏甚推重之，號為經史笥。

translations.literal: Vice Director Jiang Si greatly esteemed him and called him a basket of classics and histories.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Director Jiang Si greatly esteemed him and called him a basket of classics and histories.

units.zh: 梁天監初，吏部尚書范雲舉懋參詳五禮，除征西鄱陽王諮議參軍，兼著作郎，待詔文德省。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tianjian under Liang, Minister of the Personnel Bureau Fan Yun recommended Mao to examine the Five Rites in detail. He was appointed Military Affairs Counselor to the Campaign West under Prince Poyang, concurrently Director of Compilation, awaiting edicts at the Wende Office.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Tianjian under Liang, Minister of the Personnel Bureau Fan Yun recommended Mao to examine the Five Rites in detail. He was appointed Military Affairs Counselor to the Campaign West under Prince Poyang, concurrently Director of Compilation, awaiting edicts at the Wende Office.

units.zh: 時有請會稽封禪者，武帝因集儒學士草封禪儀，將行焉，懋建議獨以為不可。

translations.literal: At the time someone requested a feng and shan ceremony at Kuaiji. Emperor Wu therefore gathered Confucian scholars to draft the feng and shan rites and was about to proceed. Mao alone memorialized that it was not permissible.
translations.idiomatic: At the time someone requested a feng and shan ceremony at Kuaiji. Emperor Wu therefore gathered Confucian scholars to draft the feng and shan rites and was about to proceed. Mao alone memorialized that it was not permissible.

units.zh: 博通群書，多識前代舊事，甚為南陽劉之遴所重。

translations.literal: Broadly versed in all books, he knew much of earlier generations' old affairs and was greatly esteemed by Liu Zhilin of Nanyang.
translations.idiomatic: Broadly versed in all books, he knew much of earlier generations' old affairs and was greatly esteemed by Liu Zhilin of Nanyang.

units.zh: 梁太清初，為西中郎記室，兼太常丞。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Taiqing under Liang, he served as Records Officer of the Western Palace Guard and concurrently Director of the Ministry of Ceremonies.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Taiqing under Liang, he served as Records Officer of the Western Palace Guard and concurrently Director of the Ministry of Ceremonies.

units.zh: 侯景之亂，避地郢州。

translations.literal: During the Hou Jing rebellion he fled to Yingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: During the Hou Jing rebellion he fled to Yingzhou.

units.zh: 梁太清之後，所制文筆六卷。

translations.literal: After Taiqing under Liang, his literary writings filled six scrolls.
translations.idiomatic: After Taiqing under Liang, his literary writings filled six scrolls.

units.zh: 子善心，位尚書度支侍郎。

translations.literal: His son was Shanxin, who held the post of Vice Director of the Revenue Bureau of the Imperial Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: His son Shanxin served as Vice Director of the Revenue Bureau of the Imperial Secretariat.

units.zh: 殷鈞字季和，陳郡長平人，晉荊州刺史仲堪五世孫也。

translations.literal: Yin Jun, styled Jihe, was a native of Changping in Chen Commandery, fifth-generation descendant of Zhongkan, Governor of Jingzhou under Jin.
translations.idiomatic: Yin Jun, styled Jihe, was a native of Changping in Chen Commandery and a fifth-generation descendant of Zhongkan, Governor of Jingzhou under the Jin dynasty.

units.zh: 曾祖元素，宋南康相，坐元凶事誅。

translations.literal: His great-grandfather Yuansu was Chancellor of Nankang under Song and was executed for involvement in the Crown Prince's rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather Yuansu served as Chancellor of Nankang under the Song dynasty and was executed for involvement in the Crown Prince's rebellion.

units.zh: 元素娶尚書僕射琅邪王僧朗女，生子寧早卒，寧遺腹生子叡，亦當從戮，僧朗啟孝武救之得免。

translations.literal: Yuansu married the daughter of Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat Wang Senglang of Langya and had a son Ning who died early. Ning's posthumous son was Rui, who was also to be executed along with him. Senglang memorialized Emperor Xiaowu to save him and he escaped.
translations.idiomatic: Yuansu married the daughter of Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat Wang Senglang of Langya and had a son Ning who died early. Ning's posthumous son was Rui, who was also to be executed along with him. Senglang memorialized Emperor Xiaowu to save him, and he escaped.

units.zh: 叡有口辯，司徒褚彥回甚重之，謂曰：「諸殷自荊州以來無出卿。」

translations.literal: Rui had eloquence in debate. Minister of Works Chu Yanhui greatly valued him and said: "Among all the Yin clan since Jingzhou, none surpasses you."
translations.idiomatic: Rui was eloquent in debate. Minister of Works Chu Yanhui greatly valued him and said, "Among all the Yin clan since Jingzhou, none surpasses you."

units.zh: 梁武帝與叡少故舊，以女永興公主妻鈞，拜駙馬都尉。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu of Liang and Rui were old friends from youth; he gave his daughter Princess Yongxing in marriage to Jun and appointed him Commandant of the Horse Guards for the Son-in-Law.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu of Liang and Rui were old friends from youth. He gave his daughter Princess Yongxing in marriage to Jun and appointed him Commandant of the Horse Guards for the Son-in-Law.

units.zh: 曆秘書丞，在職啟校定秘閣四部書，更為目錄。

translations.literal: He successively served as Director of the Secretariat and, while in office, memorialized to collate and fix the four divisions of books in the Secret Archive and make a new catalog.
translations.idiomatic: He successively served as Director of the Secretariat and, while in office, memorialized to collate and fix the four divisions of books in the Secret Archive and make a new catalog.

units.zh: 又受詔料檢西省法書古跡，列為品目。

translations.literal: He also received an edict to examine and inspect ancient traces of model calligraphy in the Western Office and arrange them into grades and categories.
translations.idiomatic: He also received an edict to examine and inspect ancient traces of model calligraphy in the Western Office and arrange them into grades and categories.

units.zh: 幼而廬江何憲見之，深相歎賞。

translations.literal: In youth He Xian of Lujiang saw him and deeply sighed in admiration.
translations.idiomatic: In youth He Xian of Lujiang saw him and deeply sighed in admiration.

units.zh: 天監中，位秘書監、司徒左長史。

translations.literal: In the Tianjian era he held the posts of Director of the Palace Library and Left Chief Clerk to the Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: In the Tianjian era he held the posts of Director of the Palace Library and Left Chief Clerk to the Minister of Works.

units.zh: 後直東宮學士省，卒。

translations.literal: Later he served in the Eastern Palace Scholars Office and died.
translations.idiomatic: Later he served in the Eastern Palace Scholars Office and died.

units.zh: 列傳第二十九

translations.literal: Biographies 29
translations.idiomatic: the twenty-ninth year of Biography

units.zh: 殷孝祖劉勉

translations.literal: Yin Xiaozu, Liu Mian
translations.idiomatic: Yin Xiaozu and Liu Mian

primaryChapterContexts.selection: Every proposed unit plus all repeated potentially affected Chinese and English forms from the entire current chapter, with adjacent context. Full chapter was mechanically searched; other source units are outside this focused repair.

units.zh: 遷始興王前將軍安西諮議，領冠軍錄事參軍，轉司徒從事中郎，遷右長史。

translations.literal: He was transferred to advisory officer under the Prince of Shixing as Forward General and General Pacifying the West, concurrently Recorder on the staff of the Champion; transferred to Attendant of the Minister of State Affairs, then transferred to Right Chief Clerk.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to advisory officer on the staff of the Prince of Shixing as Forward General and General Pacifying the West, concurrently as Recorder on the staff of the Champion, then Attendant of the Minister of State Affairs, and finally Right Chief Clerk.

units.zh: 時陳郡謝朏爲左長史，府公竟陵王子良謂王融曰：「我府二上佐，求之前世，誰可爲比？」

translations.literal: At the time Xie Tiao of Chen commandery was Left Chief Clerk; the Prince of the headquarters, the Prince of Jingling, Ziliang, said to Wang Rong: "My headquarters' two senior aides—searching through past ages, with whom can they be compared?"
translations.idiomatic: At the time Xie Tiao of Chen served as Left Chief Clerk; the Prince of Jingling, Ziliang, said to Wang Rong: "My headquarters' two senior aides—searching through past ages, with whom can they be compared?"

units.zh: 融曰：「兩賢同時，便是未有前例。」

translations.literal: Rong said: "Two worthies at once—that in itself has no precedent."
translations.idiomatic: Wang Rong replied: "Two such worthies serving together—that in itself has no precedent."

units.zh: 晉丹陽太守沖之八世孫。

translations.literal: He was the eighth-generation descendant of Chongzhi, Administrator of Danyang under Jin.
translations.idiomatic: He was an eighth-generation descendant of Jin's Danyang administrator Chongzhi.

units.zh: 曾祖遙之，宋尚書水部郎。

translations.literal: His great-grandfather Yaozhi was Water Section Director in the Song Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather Yaozhi had been Water Section Director under the Song.

units.zh: 父珮，齊廬陵王記室參軍，早卒。

translations.literal: His father Pei was Secretary to Prince of Luling of Qi and died early.
translations.idiomatic: His father Pei, a secretary in the household of Qi's Prince of Luling, died young.

units.zh: 觀其此對，足稱王佐之才。」

translations.literal: Judging from this response, he is fully worthy to be called talent fit to assist a king."
translations.idiomatic: From this answer alone, he clearly has the makings of a king's right-hand man."

units.zh: 琅邪王融雅相友善，乃薦之於司徒竟陵王，爲西邸學士。

translations.literal: Wang Rong of Langya was on friendly terms with him and recommended him to Minister of Works Prince of Jingling, where he became a scholar of the Western Pavilion.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Rong of Langya, who knew him well, recommended him to Minister of Works Prince of Jingling, and he entered the Western Pavilion as a scholar.

units.zh: 梁臺建，與南陽劉之遴同爲太學博士，當時以爲美選。

translations.literal: When the Liang platform was established, he and Liu Zhilin of Nanyang both became Masters of the Imperial Academy—a choice then regarded as fine.
translations.idiomatic: When the Liang regime was founded, he and Nanyang's Liu Zhilin were both appointed Masters of the Imperial Academy—an appointment everyone envied.

units.zh: 休源初到京，寓於宗人少府卿孔登宅，曾以祠事入廟，侍中范雲一與相遇，深加褒賞，曰：「不期忽覯清顏，頓袪鄙吝，觀天披霧，驗之今日。」

translations.literal: When Xiuyuan first arrived in the capital he lodged at the home of his clansman Kong Deng, Junior Director of the Imperial Treasury. Once, entering a temple on sacrificial business, he met Attendant-in-Ordinary Fan Yun, who greatly praised him: "To meet your refined countenance unexpectedly dispels my baseness; parting clouds to see the heavens—verified today."
translations.idiomatic: On first reaching the capital he stayed with his kinsman Kong Deng, Junior Director of the Treasury. During a temple visit for sacrifice he met Attendant Fan Yun, who exclaimed: "I never expected to see such a clear face—it sweeps away my vulgarity, like clouds parting to reveal the sky."

units.zh: 後雲命駕到少府門，登便拂筵整帶，謂當詣己，旣而獨造休源，高談盡日，同載還家，登深以爲愧。

translations.literal: Later Yun ordered his carriage to the Junior Director's gate; Deng hastened to arrange the feast and straighten his sash, expecting Yun had come for him—but Yun went alone to Xiuyuan, talked at length all day, and returned home sharing the same carriage; Deng was deeply ashamed.
translations.idiomatic: Later Yun drove to the Junior Director's gate. Deng hurried to set out cushions and straighten his sash, sure the visit was for him. Instead Yun sought out Xiuyuan alone, talked all day, and rode home with him—leaving Deng deeply mortified.

units.zh: 尚書令沈約當朝貴顯，軒蓋盈門，休源或時後來，必虛襟引接，處之坐右，商略文義。

translations.literal: Chief Minister Shen Yue held great influence at court, his gateway always crowded with visitors; whenever Xiuyuan arrived late, Yue would always receive him with an open mind, seat him at his right hand, and discuss literary meaning.
translations.idiomatic: Chief Minister Shen Yue, then at the height of power with a constant throng at his gate, always made room for Xiuyuan when he came late, seated him on the right, and debated texts with him.

units.zh: 俄除臨川王府行參軍。

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed Adjunct in the Princely Household of Prince of Linchuan.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made an adjutant in Prince of Linchuan's household.

units.zh: 高祖嘗問吏部尚書徐勉曰：「今帝業初基，須一人有學藝解朝儀者，爲尚書儀曹郎。

translations.literal: The Emperor once asked Minister of Personnel Xu Mian: "Now that imperial enterprise is newly founded, we need someone learned in the arts who understands court rites to serve as Director of Ritual in the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu once asked Xu Mian, Minister of Personnel: "The dynasty is just taking shape. I need a learned man who knows court ceremony for Director of Ritual in the Masters of Writing.

units.zh: 爲朕思之，誰堪其選？」

translations.literal: Think for me—who is fit for this choice?"
translations.idiomatic: Think for me—who can fill the post?"

units.zh: 勉對曰：「孔休源識具清通，諳練故實，自晉、宋《起居注》誦略上口。」

translations.literal: Mian replied: "Kong Xiuyuan has clear, thorough knowledge and is versed in antiquity; the Jin and Song Daily Records he can recite from memory nearly word for word."
translations.idiomatic: Mian answered: "Kong Xiuyuan is lucid, well grounded in precedent, and can recite the Jin and Song Daily Records almost by heart."

units.zh: 高祖亦素聞之，卽日除兼尚書儀曹郎中。

translations.literal: The Emperor too had long heard of him and the same day appointed him Acting Director of Ritual in the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu had already heard of him and appointed him Acting Director of Ritual that very day.

units.zh: 是時多所改作，每逮訪前事，休源卽以所誦記隨機斷決，曾無疑滯。

translations.literal: At that time many reforms were underway; whenever they consulted him on past precedents, Xiuyuan decided on the spot from what he had memorized, never hesitating in doubt.
translations.idiomatic: The court was then revising many institutions; whenever old precedents were needed, Xiuyuan answered from memory on the spot, never at a loss.

units.zh: 吏部郎任昉常謂之爲「孔獨誦」。

translations.literal: Personnel Section Director Ren Fang often called him "Kong Who Recites Alone."
translations.idiomatic: Ren Fang of the Personnel Section nicknamed him "Kong the Sole Reciter."

units.zh: 遷建康獄正，及辨訟折獄，時罕冤人。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Corrector of Jiankang Prison; in judging lawsuits and deciding cases, rarely was anyone wrongly convicted.
translations.idiomatic: Promoted to Corrector of Jiankang Prison, he heard cases with such care that wrongful convictions were rare.

units.zh: 後有選人爲獄司者，高祖尚引休源以勵之。

translations.literal: Later when someone was chosen for prison duty, the Emperor still cited Xiuyuan as an example to encourage them.
translations.idiomatic: When a successor was later chosen for the prison post, Gaozu still held Xiuyuan up as the model.

units.zh: 除中書舍人，司徒臨川王府記室參軍，遷尚書左丞，彈肅禮闈，雅允朝望。

translations.literal: Appointed Palace Secretary, Secretary to Prince of Linchuan's household, promoted to Left Assistant Director in the Masters of Writing—in the Rites Gate he was stern and upright, fully meeting the court's expectations.
translations.idiomatic: He became Palace Secretary and secretary to Prince of Linchuan, then Left Assistant Director of the Masters of Writing, where his stern integrity in the examination hall won wide respect.

units.zh: 時太子詹事周舍撰《禮疑義》，自漢魏至于齊梁，並皆搜采，休源所有奏議，咸預編錄。

translations.literal: At that time the Crown Prince's Steward Zhou She compiled "Doubts on Rites," searching materials from Han and Wei through Qi and Liang; Xiuyuan's memorials and deliberations were all included in the compilation.
translations.idiomatic: When Crown Prince's Steward Zhou She compiled Doubts on Rites, drawing on Han, Wei, Qi, and Liang, every memorial and opinion Xiuyuan had written was included.

units.zh: 除給事黃門侍郎，遷長兼御史中丞，正色直繩，無所回避，百僚莫不憚之。

translations.literal: Appointed Supervising Gentleman-in-Attendance of the Yellow Gate, promoted to Senior Concurrent Supervisor of Censors—in upright color and straight measure he deferred to nothing; all officials feared him.
translations.idiomatic: Made Supervising Gentleman of the Yellow Gate and then Senior Concurrent Censor, he was unflinching in enforcing the law, and the whole bureaucracy feared him.

units.zh: 除少府卿，又兼行丹陽尹事。

translations.literal: Appointed Junior Director of the Imperial Treasury, additionally acting as Magistrate of Danyang.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Junior Director of the Treasury and also acted as magistrate of Danyang.

units.zh: 出爲宣惠晉安王府長史、南郡太守、行荊州府州事。

translations.literal: He went out as Chief of the Princely Household of Propagation and Grace Prince of Jin'an, Administrator of Nan commandery, directing Jing province military and civil affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He left the capital as chief secretary to Propagation and Grace Prince of Jin'an, administrator of Nan commandery, with charge of Jingzhou affairs.

units.zh: 高祖深嘉之。

translations.literal: The Emperor deeply commended this.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu praised him warmly for it.

units.zh: 除通直散騎常侍，領羽林監，轉秘書監，遷明威將軍，復爲晉安王府長史、南蘭陵太守，別敕專行南徐州事。

translations.literal: Appointed Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry, overseeing the Feathered Forest Guard, transferred to Director of the Secretariat, promoted to Bright Might General, again Chief of Jin'an's household and Administrator of South Lanling—separate edict put him solely in charge of South Xu affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He became Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry and head of the Feathered Forest Guard, then Director of the Secretariat and Bright Might General, again chief secretary to Prince of Jin'an and administrator of South Lanling, with a special commission for South Xu alone.

units.zh: 休源累佐名籓，甚得民譽，王深相倚仗，軍民機務，動止詢謀。

translations.literal: Xiuyuan had repeatedly assisted famous fiefs, winning great popular repute; the prince deeply relied on him—military and civilian urgent business, every move and halt consulted his counsel.
translations.idiomatic: Having served several great princely domains, he enjoyed wide public esteem; the prince leaned on him heavily, consulting him on every military and civil decision.

units.zh: 官至岳陽王府諮議、東揚州別駕。

translations.literal: He reached the posts of Adviser to Prince of Yueyang's household and Deputy Governor of East Yangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to adviser in Prince of Yueyang's household and deputy governor of East Yangzhou.

units.zh: 少子宗軌，聰敏有識度，歷尚書都官郎，司徒左西掾，中書郎。

translations.literal: His youngest son Zonggui was clever and perceptive, serving as Director in the Masters of Writing's Bureau of Punishments, Left Western Aide to the Minister of Works, and Palace Secretary.
translations.idiomatic: His youngest son Zonggui was bright and discerning, and served as Director in the Bureau of Punishments, left western aide to the Minister of Works, and Palace Secretary.

units.zh: 江革，字休映，濟陽考城人也。

translations.literal: Jiang Ge, styled Xiuying, was a native of Kaocheng in Jiyang.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Ge, styled Xiuying, came from Kaocheng in Jiyang.

units.zh: 祖齊之，宋尚書金部郎。

translations.literal: His grandfather Qizhi was Gold Section Director in the Song Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Qizhi had been Gold Section Director under the Song.

units.zh: 父柔之，齊尚書倉部郎，有孝行，以母憂毀卒。

translations.literal: His father Rouzhi was Granaries Section Director under Qi, famed for filial conduct—he died from grief in mourning for his mother.
translations.idiomatic: His father Rouzhi, Granaries Section Director under Qi, was renowned for filial piety and died of grief while mourning his mother.

units.zh: 革幼而聰敏，早有才思，六歲便解屬文。

translations.literal: Ge was clever and sharp from childhood with early literary talent; at six he could already compose linked prose.
translations.idiomatic: Clever from childhood and precocious in letters, Ge could write linked prose at six.

units.zh: 服闋，與觀俱詣太學，補國子生，舉高第。

translations.literal: When mourning ended, he and Guan both went to the Imperial Academy, enrolled as a student of the National University, and were selected at the top of the class.
translations.idiomatic: After mourning he and Guan entered the Imperial Academy as National University students and graduated at the top of their class.

units.zh: 齊中書郎王融、吏部謝朓雅相欽重。

translations.literal: Qi Palace Secretary Wang Rong and Personnel Director Xie Tiao both held him in high regard.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Rong, Palace Secretary of Qi, and Xie Tiao, Director of Personnel, both admired him.

units.zh: 朓嘗宿衛，還過候革，時大雪，見革弊絮單席，而耽學不倦，嗟歎久之，乃脫所著襦，並手割半氈與革充臥具而去。

translations.literal: Tiao once returned from palace guard duty and visited Ge; it was snowing heavily—seeing Ge in worn cotton with only a thin mat yet studying without tiring, Tiao sighed for a long time, took off the padded jacket he wore, and with his own hands cut half a felt mat for Ge's bedding before leaving.
translations.idiomatic: Once, coming off palace guard duty in heavy snow, Tiao visited Ge and found him in patched cotton on a thin mat, still studying without pause. Tiao sighed long, gave him the padded jacket he was wearing, and cut half his felt mat by hand for Ge's bedding before he left.

units.zh: 司徒竟陵王聞其名，引爲西邸學士。

translations.literal: Minister of Works Prince of Jingling heard his fame and brought him in as a Western Pavilion scholar.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Jingling, Minister of Works, heard of him and made him a Western Pavilion scholar.

units.zh: 弱冠舉南徐州秀才。

translations.literal: At weak-cap age he was selected as xiucai of South Xu province.
translations.idiomatic: At twenty he was chosen xiucai of South Xu province.

units.zh: 祏誅，賓客皆罹其罪，革獨以智免。

translations.literal: When Shi was executed, his guests all suffered in his crime; Ge alone escaped through wit.
translations.idiomatic: When Shi was executed, every man in his circle was implicated; Ge alone escaped through cleverness.

units.zh: 除尚書駕部郎。

translations.literal: Appointed Driving Section Director in the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Driving Section Director in the Masters of Writing.

units.zh: 中興元年，高祖入石頭，時吳興太守袁昂據郡距義師，乃使革制書與昂，于坐立成，辭義典雅，高祖深賞歎之，因令與徐勉同掌書記。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhongxing the Emperor entered Stone Fort; at that time Yuan Ang, Administrator of Wuxing, held the commandery against the righteous army—Ge was sent to compose the imperial letter to Ang and finished it standing at the desk; its phrasing was elegant and classical, and the Emperor deeply admired it, then had him jointly manage written records with Xu Mian.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Zhongxing Gaozu entered Stone Fort while Yuan Ang, administrator of Wuxing, held the commandery against the cause. Ge was told to draft the letter to Ang and finished it on the spot; its language was elegant, Gaozu praised it highly, and put him in charge of written records together with Xu Mian.

units.zh: 爲治明肅，豪強憚之。

translations.literal: His governance was clear and stern—the powerful feared him.
translations.idiomatic: He governed with clarity and severity, and the local strongmen feared him.

units.zh: 入爲中書舍人，尚書左丞，司農卿，復出爲雲麾晉安王長史、尋陽太守、行江州府事。

translations.literal: He entered as Palace Writer Attendant, Left Assistant Director of the Ministry of Works, and Minister of Agriculture; then went out again as Chief Clerk to Prince Jin'an of Cloud Banner, Administrator of Xunyang, and overseer of Jiangzhou prefectural affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He entered court as Palace Writer Attendant, Left Assistant Director of the Masters of Writing, and Minister of Agriculture, then went out again as chief clerk to Prince Jin'an of Cloud Banner, administrator of Xunyang, and acting head of Jiangzhou affairs.

units.zh: 徙仁威廬陵王長史，太守、行事如故，以清嚴爲百城所憚。

translations.literal: He was transferred as Chief Clerk to Prince Renwei of Luling; his posts as administrator and acting deputy remained unchanged, and every commandery feared him for his probity and severity.
translations.idiomatic: Transferred to chief clerk for Prince Renwei of Luling, he kept the same administrator and acting duties, and commanderies across the realm feared his austerity.

units.zh: 每至侍宴，言論必以《詩》《書》，王因此耽學好文。

translations.literal: Whenever he attended banquets, his talk always drew on the Odes and Documents; the Prince therefore devoted himself to study and letters.
translations.idiomatic: At every banquet his talk turned to the Odes and Documents, and the prince came to love learning and letters.

units.zh: 典簽沈熾文以王所制詩呈高祖，高祖謂僕射徐勉曰：「江革果能稱職。」

translations.literal: Chief of Staff Shen Chiwen presented the Prince's poems to Gaozu; Gaozu said to Vice Director Xu Mian: "Jiang Ge has indeed proved equal to his charge."
translations.idiomatic: Chief of staff Shen Chiwen showed the prince's poems to Gaozu. Gaozu told Vice Director Xu Mian, "Jiang Ge has truly done his duty."

units.zh: 乃除都官尚書。

translations.literal: Appointed Minister of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Minister of Justice.

units.zh: 好獎進閭閻，爲後生延譽，由是衣冠士子，翕然歸之。

translations.literal: He loved to encourage village folk and build reputations for the young—therefore gentry and scholars flocked to him.
translations.idiomatic: He loved to lift up common folk and speak well of the young, and gentry and scholars gathered to him.

units.zh: 時尚書令何敬容掌選，序用多非其人。

translations.literal: Minister of Works He Jingrong controlled appointments; the ranked selections were often unworthy.
translations.idiomatic: Minister of Works He Jingrong controlled appointments, and many of his choices were unworthy.

units.zh: 革性強直，每至朝宴，恒有褒貶，以此爲權勢所疾，乃謝病還家。

translations.literal: Ge was by nature forceful and upright; at every court banquet he always had praise and blame—therefore the powerful hated him, and he pleaded illness and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: Ge was forceful and upright. At every court banquet he praised and blamed without restraint. The powerful resented him, and he pleaded illness and went home.

units.zh: 次子從簡，少有文情，年十七，作《采荷詞》以刺敬容，爲當時所賞。

translations.literal: Second son Congjian had literary sensibility from youth; at seventeen he wrote "Song of Gathering Lotus" to satirize Jingrong and won acclaim in his day.
translations.idiomatic: Second son Congjian had literary feeling from youth. At seventeen he wrote "Song of Gathering Lotus" to satirize Jingrong, and his age praised it.

units.zh: 歷官司徒從事中郎。

translations.literal: He served as aide to the Minister of Education.
translations.idiomatic: He served as aide to the Minister of Education.

units.zh: 侯景亂，爲任約所害。

translations.literal: In Hou Jing's rebellion he was killed by Ren Yue.
translations.idiomatic: In Hou Jing's rebellion Ren Yue killed him.

translations.literal: The taboo name of Emperor Cheng was Yan, his courtesy name Shigen, and he was the eldest son of Emperor Ming.
